descriptionChirho: A masculine noun (אַרְיֵה) denoting a lion, one of several Hebrew words for lion (cf. כְּפִיר 'young lion,' לָבִיא 'lioness,' שַׁחַל 'fierce lion'). Used both literally of the animal (Judg 14:5–8, 1 Sam 17:34–36, 1 Kgs 13:24–28, 2 Kgs 17:25–26, Dan 6) and in simile/metaphor for strength, ferocity, or predatory danger (Gen 49:9, Num 24:9, Ps 7:3, 10:9, 17:12, 22:14, Prov 22:13, 26:13, Isa 31:4, Hos 5:14, Amos 3:8). The three clusters represent: the noun with various prefixes—bare, with article, conjunction (35x); with comparative preposition כְּ 'like a lion' (10x); and a ketiv/qere variant (1x). All are the same lexeme. Multilingual: spa león, hin सिंह, arb أَسَد, kor 사자, swa simba.
